timeline.body:
Back when we introduced queries against runtime fields, Elasticsearch did not support
inter-segment concurrency yet. At the time, it was fine to assume that segments will be
searched sequentially. AbstractStringScriptFieldAutomatonQuery used to have a BytesRefBuilder
instance shared across the segments, which gets re-initialized when each segment starts its work.
This is no longer possible with inter-segment concurrency.

Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/105911
Hi @javanna, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

@nik9000 pinging you because you wrote this in the first place. How important is it to have a pre-initialized BytesRefBuilder as opposed to creating one within matches every time? I went for the ThreadLocal initially, but I think that it's probably overkill. Do you have opinions?

reply.body: Thinking out loud: before we would create a single scratch, shared across all segments. With the thread local, we would create one per thread executing a certain query: there's a max number of threads we use for a single search, despite the number of slices may be high. Without the threadlocal, we would create a new instance for each segment.

I think it's pretty important not to allocate every time. I just fixed someone on the ESQL side that is shaped kind of similar and it went from ~25 nanos per run to ~12 nanos per run. 

If we have segment-level concurrency we could make the scratch when we make a `Scorer`.

> If we have segment-level concurrency we could make the scratch when we make a Scorer.

How would that work? The scorer is made per segment anyways?  Each thread that runs matches needs to have a different instance of the scratch, it cannot be shared, unless we want to synchronize its access, which does not seem like a good idea. That is what the thread local does: give each thread a different instance.
Yeah, Scorers are always made per segment. If we're running per-segment concurrency that's probably fine.
oh ok. Sorry, I think I had missed the you wanted to avoid creating the scratch per document. That makes sense to me. One scratch per segment or one per thread does not make a huge difference.

> One scratch per segment or one per thread does not make a huge difference.

Yeah! I really like avoiding the ThreadLocal because those are hard for me to read.
yea I tend to agree. I extended the script context, that gets created per segment, to include the scratch instance. This should do it.
err, that does not work, and reminds me once again never to mess with painless script contexts :)

timeline.message:
Fix concurrency bug in AbstractStringScriptFieldAutomatonQuery

Back when we introduced queries against runtime fields, Elasticsearch did not support
inter-segment concurrency yet. At the time, it was fine to assume that segments will be
searched sequentially. AbstractStringScriptFieldAutomatonQuery used to have a BytesRefBuilder
instance shared across the segments, which gets re-initialized when each segment starts its work.
This is no longer possible with inter-segment concurrency.

Closes #105911

timeline.body: These concurrency test are kind of artificial now that they rely on the different matches method... we could rely on integration tests perhaps instead.

reply.body: If you built a `Scorer` or something that could work. That's kind of integration-y. You'd need to make a lucene index, but sometimes that's life.

Yep, I later realized that we already have coverage for all of this in our script field type tests. Only, those did not leverage concurrency as we never ended up running them against multiple segments. I have added an addDocument method to the base class that more aggressively flushes, this is ok as we are only ever adding a few documents. The random flush within RandomIndexWriter needs a minimum number of 10 docs which is never reached in these tests.
With this adjustment, I was able to reproduce the problem and ensure that it is now fixed.
